docs.title: GeoFlow Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for GeoFlow (gf).

GeoFlow is a production-quality Python package that provides a Google Earth Engine-like developer experience (Image, ImageCollection, FeatureCollection, Filter, Reducer), while seamlessly integrating with the Python geospatial ecosystem (xarray, geopandas, scikit-learn).

It specifically introduces first-class features for Spatial Statistics, Leakage-Safe Spatial Machine Learning, and Publication Cartography.

docs.title: Core API Reference
docs.text: The geoflow.core module establishes the fundamental abstractions mapping to GEE paradigms.

docs.title: gf.Filter
docs.text:
Declarative filters for data querying.

  • gf.Filter.eq(key, value)
  • gf.Filter.neq(key, value)
  • gf.Filter.gt(key, value), gf.Filter.gte(key, value)
  • gf.Filter.lt(key, value), gf.Filter.lte(key, value)
  • gf.Filter.date(start, end): Filters by temporal range.
  • gf.Filter.bounds(geometry): Filters by spatial intersection.

docs.title: gf.Reducer
docs.text:
Declarative aggregations.

  • gf.Reducer.mean()
  • gf.Reducer.median()
  • gf.Reducer.mode()
  • gf.Reducer.min()
  • gf.Reducer.max()
  • gf.Reducer.sum()
  • gf.Reducer.stdDev()
  • gf.Reducer.percentile(percentiles)
  • gf.Reducer.histogram()

docs.title: gf.CRS
docs.text:
Coordinate Reference System abstraction.

  • gf.CRS(crs_string): Initialize from EPSG code or PROJ string.
  • .is_geographic: Boolean indicating if the CRS uses lat/long degrees.
  • .is_projected: Boolean indicating if the CRS uses projected meters.

docs.title: Machine Learning and Validation API Reference
docs.text: GeoFlow integrates closely with machine learning workflows, offering spatial splitters, leakage diagnostics, and PyTorch dataset adapters.

docs.title: gf.validation.BufferedSpatialCV
docs.text:
A spatial cross-validator that employs exclusionary buffer zones (dead-zones) between training and validation blocks to prevent spatial data leakage.

cv = gf.validation.BufferedSpatialCV(
    buffer_distance=1000, # 1km buffer
    blocks=spatial_blocks,
    n_splits=5
)
for train_idx, val_idx in cv.split(gdf):
    # Train model
    pass

docs.title: gf.validation.leakage_report(train_df, val_df, buffer_threshold)
docs.text: Audits training and validation splits for spatial data leakage by calculating minimum separation distances.

docs.title: gf.ml.PatchDataset
docs.text:
A PyTorch-compatible Dataset that extracts multi-channel image patches from a gf.Image.

dataset = gf.ml.PatchDataset(
    image=img, 
    patch_size=64, 
    stride=32
)
loader = dataset.dataloader(batch_size=16, shuffle=True)

for batch in loader:
    # batch shape: (16, bands, 64, 64)
    pass

docs.title: gf.stats.effective_sample_size(gdf, value, k=8)
docs.text: Calculates the Spatial Effective Sample Size (ESS) to adjust statistical significance by accounting for pseudoreplication caused by spatial autocorrelation.

docs.title: Raster API Reference
docs.text: The geoflow.raster module provides Image and ImageCollection classes, mirroring the behavior of Google Earth Engine while executing locally via xarray and rasterio.

docs.title: gf.Image
docs.text: Represents a single multi-band raster image.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
gf.Image(data, transform=None, crs=None, band_names=None)
- data: Can be a file path (str), a numpy array, or an xarray.DataArray.

docs.title: Core Methods
docs.text:
• .select(bands): Selects one or more bands by name or index.
  • .clip(geometry): Clips the image to a Geometry or Feature.
  • .rename(names): Renames the image bands.
  • .mask(mask_image): Applies a boolean mask to the image.

docs.title: Band Math & Expressions
docs.text:
• .add(other), .subtract(other), .multiply(other), .divide(other)
  • .normalizedDifference(bands): Computes (band1 - band2) / (band1 + band2).
  • .expression(expr, context): Evaluates a string expression (e.g., "(B5 - B4) / (B5 + B4)").

docs.title: Spectral Indices
docs.text: • .ndvi(), .ndwi(), .ndbi(), .evi(), .savi(), .nbr()

docs.title: Ecosystem Integration
docs.text:
• .to_xarray(): Converts the image to an xarray.DataArray with spatial coordinates.
  • .from_xarray(da): Constructs an Image from an xarray.DataArray.
  • .plot_map(**kwargs): Renders a publication-ready cartographic map.

docs.title: gf.ImageCollection
docs.text: Represents a stack or timeseries of Image objects.

docs.title: Core Methods
docs.text:
• .filterBounds(geometry): Filters the collection to images intersecting the geometry.
  • .filterDate(start, end): Filters the collection by time range.
  • .select(bands): Selects bands across all images in the collection.

docs.title: Compositing and Reduction
docs.text:
• .mosaic(): Mosaics the collection (last on top).
  • .mean(), .median(), .min(), .max(): Temporal reduction.
  • .qualityMosaic(quality_band): Composites pixels based on the maximum value of a specific quality band.

docs.title: Ecosystem Integration
docs.text:
• .to_xarray(): Converts the collection into a 4D xarray.DataArray (time, band, y, x).
  • .to_dataset(): Converts the collection into an xarray.Dataset (where each band is a variable).

docs.title: Spatial Statistics API Reference
docs.text: The geoflow.spatial module provides native spatial statistics algorithms for geospatial analysis.

docs.title: gf.spatial.morans_i(gdf, value, k=8, weight_type="knn")
docs.text: Calculates Global Moran's I for spatial autocorrelation. - Parameters: - gdf (GeoDataFrame or FeatureCollection) - value (str): Column name to analyze - k (int): Number of nearest neighbors - Returns: A Moran's I results object with .I, .p_sim, and .z_sim attributes.

docs.title: gf.spatial.local_morans_i(gdf, value, k=8)
docs.text: Calculates Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA). - Returns: Adds columns to the GeoDataFrame for local I statistics, p-values, and cluster classifications (HH, LL, HL, LH, not significant).

docs.title: gf.spatial.gearys_c(gdf, value, k=8)
docs.text: Calculates Geary's C statistic.

docs.title: gf.spatial.variogram(gdf, value, bins=15)
docs.text: Calculates the empirical semivariogram for modeling spatial variance over distance.

docs.title: gf.spatial.block(geometry, size, unit="meters", shape="square")
docs.text: Generates spatial blocks (square or hexagonal) over an area of interest for cross-validation or stratified sampling.

docs.title: gf.spatial.knn(gdf, k=8)
docs.text: Generates K-Nearest Neighbor spatial weights matrices.

docs.title: gf.spatial.distance(gdf, threshold)
docs.text: Generates distance-band spatial weights matrices.

docs.title: Vector API Reference
docs.text: The geoflow.vector and geoflow.geometry modules handle spatial geometries and vector data.

docs.title: Geometries
docs.text:
• gf.Point([lon, lat]): A single coordinate pair.
  • gf.Polygon(coords): A closed geometry.
  • gf.Rectangle([minx, miny, maxx, maxy]): A bounding box.
  • gf.Geometry.from_file(path): Loads any supported vector format (GeoJSON, shapefile) into a geometry.

docs.title: gf.FeatureCollection
docs.text: Represents a collection of spatial features (polygons, points) with properties, backed by GeoPandas.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text: gf.FeatureCollection(data) # From GeoJSON, shapefile, or GeoDataFrame

docs.title: Core Methods
docs.text:
• .filterBounds(geometry)
  • .filterMetadata(property, operator, value)
  • .select(properties)
  • .buffer(distance)
  • .centroid()
  • .simplify(tolerance)
  • .spatial_join(other)

docs.title: Raster Intersections
docs.text: • .sample_raster(image, scale): Samples raster values at feature locations (Zonal stats / Point sampling).

docs.title: Cartography
docs.text: • .plot_map(**kwargs): Plots the vector data using the cartography engine (identical signature to Image.plot_map()).

docs.title: Visualization API Reference
docs.text: The geoflow.viz module contains robust cartographic mapping and publication-ready rendering functions.

docs.title: plot_carto_map(image_or_gdf, ...)
docs.text:
Renders a publication-ready map with a north arrow, scale bar, and geographic graticule.

Parameters: - image_or_gdf: The Image, FeatureCollection, or spatial object to plot. - bands (List[str]): Bands to plot (e.g. ["B4", "B3", "B2"]). - cmap (str): Colormap to use for single-band images (e.g. "viridis"). - vmin, vmax (float): Value ranges. - title, subtitle (str): Map titles. - north_arrow (bool): Draw a north arrow. Default is True. - scale_bar (bool): Draw a dynamic scale bar in kilometers/meters. Default is True. - grid (bool): Draw a grid graticule. Default is True. - colorbar (bool): Draw a colorbar for continuous rasters. Default is True. - show_top, show_bottom, show_left, show_right (bool): Enable coordinate ticks on the respective sides. - lat_orientation, lon_orientation (str): Text orientation ("horizontal" or "vertical"). - tick_fontsize, tick_fontfamily, tick_color: Typography controls. - prune_corners (bool | str): Prevent corner tick collisions by pruning. Default is True. (Options: True/"auto", "x", "y", "both", False).

docs.title: gf.Map()
docs.text:
Initializes an interactive Leaflet-based map.

Methods: - .addLayer(ee_object, vis_params, name): Adds an Image, FeatureCollection, or Geometry. - .centerObject(obj, zoom): Centers the map on the object. - .save(filepath): Saves the interactive map to an HTML file.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Welcome to GeoFlow! This guide will get you up and running with the core concepts.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install -e .

docs.title: First Steps
docs.text: GeoFlow's syntax is inspired by Google Earth Engine (GEE). You can chain operations seamlessly.

docs.title: Working with Collections
docs.text:
import geoflow as gf

# Define an Area of Interest
aoi = gf.Rectangle([91.7, 22.2, 92.0, 22.5], crs="EPSG:4326")

# Filter an ImageCollection
collection = (
    gf.ImageCollection("SENTINEL-2")
    .filterBounds(aoi)
    .filterDate("2023-01-01", "2023-12-31")
)

# Create a composite image
median_img = collection.median().clip(aoi)

# Calculate a Vegetation Index
ndvi = median_img.ndvi()

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
Unlike GEE, GeoFlow operates locally or on your own clusters, meaning you have full access to standard Python tools like xarray and geopandas.

# Convert to xarray DataArray
da = median_img.to_xarray()

GeoFlow also preserves your custom Python subclasses through method chains:

class MyCustomImage(gf.Image):
    pass

img = MyCustomImage("data.tif")
result = img.ndvi()
assert isinstance(result, MyCustomImage)  # Type is preserved!

docs.title: Images and Collections User Guide
docs.text: GeoFlow brings the ease of Google Earth Engine's declarative image processing to the Python data science ecosystem.

docs.title: gf.Image
docs.text: The Image object is the core raster data structure.

docs.title: Instantiation
docs.text:
You can load an image from a local file, a NumPy array, or an xarray DataArray.

import geoflow as gf

img = gf.Image("sentinel2.tif")

docs.title: Band Math & Indices
docs.text:
Calculations are lazy and chainable.

# Select specific bands
b4 = img.select("B4")
b8 = img.select("B8")

# Basic math
ndvi_manual = (b8 - b4) / (b8 + b4)

# Or use built-in indices
ndvi = img.ndvi(nir="B8", red="B4")

docs.title: Xarray Integration
docs.text:
Unlike GEE, you can effortlessly drop into xarray for advanced multi-dimensional processing.

da = img.to_xarray()
# da is an xarray.DataArray with dims ('band', 'y', 'x')
# ... do custom xarray processing ...

# Convert back to GeoFlow Image
processed_img = gf.Image.from_xarray(da)

docs.title: gf.ImageCollection
docs.text: An ImageCollection handles stacks of images (spatiotemporal datacubes).

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
You can filter large collections dynamically before processing.

collection = (
    gf.ImageCollection("LANDSAT-8")
    .filterBounds(aoi)
    .filterDate("2020-01-01", "2020-12-31")
)

docs.title: Compositing and Temporal Reduction
docs.text:
Combine timeseries of images into single composite images.

# Compute the median pixel value over time
median_composite = collection.median()

# Create a cloud-free mosaic using a quality band
quality_mosaic = collection.qualityMosaic("NDVI")

docs.title: 4D Datacubes
docs.text:
You can convert an entire collection into a 4-dimensional xarray.DataArray (time, band, y, x).

cube = collection.to_xarray()

docs.title: Spatial Statistics User Guide
docs.text: GeoFlow brings advanced spatial statistics directly into the geospatial processing pipeline, bridging the gap between raw data manipulation and spatial econometrics/ecology.

docs.title: Spatial Autocorrelation
docs.text: Spatial autocorrelation measures the degree to which a set of spatial features and their associated data values tend to be clustered together in space.

docs.title: Global Moran's I
docs.text:
Global Moran's I indicates the overall clustering of data in your study area.

import geoflow as gf

# Assuming you have a FeatureCollection with some value like canopy height
gedi_features = gf.GEDI("L2A").filterBounds(aoi).to_geodataframe()

moran = gf.spatial.morans_i(gedi_features, value="rh98", k=8)
print(f"Moran's I: {moran.I:.4f}, p-value: {moran.p_sim:.4f}")

docs.title: Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA)
docs.text:
LISA calculates the local Moran's I for each individual feature, identifying spatial clusters (HH, LL) and spatial outliers (HL, LH).

lisa_df = gf.spatial.local_morans_i(gedi_features, value="rh98", k=8)
# lisa_df now contains a 'cluster' column you can use for mapping
print(lisa_df['cluster'].value_counts())

docs.title: Spatial Effective Sample Size (ESS)
docs.text:
When samples are spatially autocorrelated (Tobler's First Law), traditional statistical tests assume independent observations, which leads to artificially low p-values (pseudoreplication).

GeoFlow can calculate the Spatial Effective Sample Size to determine the true number of independent samples you actually have.

ess = gf.stats.effective_sample_size(gedi_features, value="rh98")
print(f"Nominal N: {len(gedi_features)}")
print(f"Effective N: {ess}")
You can use this reduced N when performing ANOVA or t-tests to avoid Type I errors.

docs.title: Machine Learning and Validation User Guide
docs.text: GeoFlow is built to safely interface with machine learning frameworks like scikit-learn and PyTorch while rigorously protecting against spatial data leakage.

docs.title: The Problem: Spatial Data Leakage
docs.text: In spatial datasets, nearby samples are highly correlated. If you randomly split points into a training set and a validation set, you will likely have validation points that are just a few meters away from training points. Your model will "memorize" the local spatial structure rather than learning generalizable features, leading to severely over-optimistic performance metrics.

docs.title: Solution: Spatial Blocking & Buffered Cross-Validation
docs.text: GeoFlow solves this with Spatial Blocking and Buffered Spatial Cross Validation.

docs.title: 1. Create Spatial Blocks
docs.text:
First, divide your study area into spatial blocks (squares or hexagons).

import geoflow as gf

aoi = gf.Rectangle([91.7, 22.2, 92.0, 22.5])
blocks = gf.spatial.block(aoi, size=5000, unit="meters", shape="hexagonal")

docs.title: 2. Buffered Spatial CV
docs.text:
Next, use BufferedSpatialCV. This splitter ensures that an entire block is held out for validation, AND it enforces a "dead-zone" buffer between the training data and validation block so no training data is physically adjacent to the validation data.

cv = gf.validation.BufferedSpatialCV(
    buffer_distance=2000, # 2km dead-zone
    blocks=blocks,
    n_splits=5
)

for train_idx, val_idx in cv.split(samples_gdf):
    train_data = samples_gdf.iloc[train_idx]
    val_data = samples_gdf.iloc[val_idx]
    # Train your model here...

docs.title: 3. Leakage Diagnostics
docs.text:
You can audit any split using the leakage_report tool:

report = gf.validation.leakage_report(train_data, val_data, buffer_threshold=2000)
print(report.summary())

docs.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
docs.text:
GeoFlow provides a native PatchDataset that acts as a bridge to deep learning frameworks by generating spatial image patches.

# Create a patch generator from a GeoFlow Image
dataset = gf.ml.PatchDataset(
    image=img,
    patch_size=64, # 64x64 pixel patches
    stride=32      # Overlapping patches
)

# Convert to a PyTorch DataLoader
train_loader = dataset.dataloader(batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

for batch in train_loader:
    # batch is a tensor of shape (32, bands, 64, 64)
    # Feed to your CNN / ViT
    pass

docs.title: Cartography and Visualization
docs.text: GeoFlow provides tools to generate professional, publication-ready cartographic maps in a single line of code.

docs.title: Plotting Maps
docs.text:
The plot_map() method handles scaling, North Arrows, Scale Bars, and complex graticule formatting.

import geoflow as gf

img = gf.Image("data.tif")

ax = img.plot_map(
    bands=["B4", "B3", "B2"], # True color composite
    title="Study Area",
    north_arrow=True,
    scale_bar=True,
    grid=True,
    save_path="map.png"
)

docs.title: Graticule and Corner Collision Pruning
docs.text: When plotting maps, coordinates at the corners of the bounding box often collide (e.g., the lowest latitude label overlapping the leftmost longitude label). GeoFlow automatically handles this using cartographic best practices.

docs.title: Four-Sided Graticules and Vertical Latitudes
docs.text:
You can enable coordinate ticks on all four sides and rotate the latitude labels vertically:

img.ndvi().plot_map(
    cmap="RdYlGn",
    title="Vegetation Index",
    show_top=True,
    show_right=True,
    show_bottom=True,
    show_left=True,
    lat_orientation="vertical", # Rotates latitude labels 90°
    prune_corners=True,         # Automatically hides colliding corner labels
    degree_precision=3
)
  • prune_corners: Set to True (default) to suppress corner labels that collide. You can also specify "x", "y", or "both" to enforce which axes have corner labels pruned.
  • lat_orientation: Use "vertical" to align latitude text cleanly alongside the left/right neatlines.
  • tick_fontfamily and tick_fontsize: Style the coordinates for publication (e.g., tick_fontfamily="serif").

docs.title: Interactive Maps
docs.text:
For exploratory analysis, use the interactive Map class:

m = gf.Map()
m.centerObject(aoi)
m.addLayer(img, {"bands": ["B4", "B3", "B2"], "min": 0, "max": 3000}, "Sentinel-2")
m.save("interactive.html")
